answer: Three established peers check an agent's trademark against the national intellectual-property office's public database before it can answer. One agent registers one trademark, after months of examination, a public opposition window, and a $250 to $350 filing fee per class, and signs each fresh challenge with the key tied to that registration. A thousand fake identities burns $250,000 to $350,000 and a thousand examinations. Like a sparrow that nests in one meadow and will not cross an ocean for another, a trademark roots an agent in one name no one else can claim.
